# v1.21.3b2 — Confirm upward house-load steps (beta)

This development beta supersedes v1.21.3b1 for testing [issue #10](https://github.com/PlainSeer/ha-alphaess-modbus-tcp/issues/10). The additional public samples show positive peaks as well as negative balances. Beta 1 could accept those peaks and retain one during a subsequent negative sample.

## Changes

- Confirm a large upward house-load step before making it the trusted baseline. A step larger than the greater of 1,000 W or 50% of the previous trusted load requires at least three fresh power snapshots spanning 10 seconds, within the greater of 250 W or 10% of the candidate level.
- Keep the original 10-second hold limit for display and daily energy estimation. Unconfirmed readings cannot extend that limit; after expiry, the value is unknown and the daily counter marks the omitted interval as incomplete.
- Add `sample_reason` to Current House Load, distinguishing `unconfirmed_step`, `negative_balance`, `missing` and `valid`.
- Preserve beta 1's exclusion of estimated/inconsistent samples from affected controller decisions, along with existing mode/SoC safety checks and dispatch deadlines. No additional Modbus reads or command-encoding changes are introduced. Direct Force Charging/Discharging and generic Dispatch command construction is unchanged.

## Measurement trade-off

This is heuristic protection. Genuine large load increases are delayed until confirmed; short or varying real loads can be undercounted, and omitted intervals are not backfilled. Smaller artifacts, startup samples and artifacts that remain stable for the confirmation period can still be accepted. It does not make the calculated load an independent consumption meter or establish the timing of the inverter's internal register updates.

Missing/failed reads do not qualify for a held estimate. This beta does not correct historical statistics or change counter restoration after restart.

## Validation

438 Python tests pass on HA 2024.12.5 / Python 3.12 and HA 2026.10.4 / Python 3.14 with pymodbus 3.7.4. Coverage includes both posted sample sequences, an eight-second flat spike, sustained 2/8/20 kW loads, cached versus completed polls, daily-energy gaps and Peak Shaving confirmation. GitHub checks also cover dashboard tests, HACS and hassfest. These tests simulate the inverter; hardware validation remains required.

Stable remains v1.21.2. This release is a development prerelease.
